You're hitting **two separate Marketo gotchas**, both documented but counter-intuitive:

## Problem 1: `:default=` doesn't work on Email Script tokens

The `:default=` syntax **only works on simple tokens** like `{{lead.First Name:default=there}}`. It does **not** work on Email Script (Velocity) tokens at all. Adobe states this explicitly: *"Email Script tokens are not designed to work with the `{{my.token:default=Some Value}}` syntax, which is for simple tokens."*

So `{{my.accountManagerScript:default=our team}}` will never use that default.

## Problem 2: `$display.alt()` doesn't work on lead fields

Marketo ensures all **lead fields are Strings, never `null`**. An empty field is an empty string `""`, not `null`. 

`$display.alt()` only substitutes when a value is **actually `null`** — so it will never fire for an empty lead field. You'll get either the name or a blank, never the fallback.

## The fix: Use `.isEmpty()` inside the script

Handle the fallback **inside your Velocity** with an explicit empty-string check:

```velocity
#if( $lead.AccountManagerName.isEmpty() )
our team##
#else
$esc.html($lead.AccountManagerName)##
#end
```

The `##` at the end of each line suppresses trailing newlines. The `$esc.html()` escapes any special characters for safe HTML output.

Then reference it in your email as just `{{my.accountManagerScript}}` with no `:default=`.

---

**Why both exist:** Simple tokens get `:default=` because they have no logic. Velocity tokens get full conditional logic, so you handle fallbacks yourself with `#if`/`#else`.

**Every Marketo email is assembled using Velocity under the hood**, so these 13 strings break validation anywhere they appear — even in plain HTML with no scripting at all:

```
#if  #else  #elseif  #foreach  #end  #set  #define
#macro  #include  #parse  #break  #stop  #evaluate
```

You have `#end` in two places:

1. **The URL:** `https://example.com/legal/#end-user-agreement`
2. **Body copy:** `"to the #end"`

**In the body text** — insert a word joiner character after the `#`:
```html
to the #⁠end
```

The word joiner is invisible to the reader but breaks the reserved-word pattern for Marketo's parser.

Make those two changes and the validation error should clear.

The `#` will render as `#` in the browser/email client, but Marketo's Velocity parser won't see it as a script directive.

This is a common gotcha with Marketo emails — any text that looks like a Velocity directive (`#if`, `#else`, `#end`, `#foreach`, etc.) will trigger validation errors even in plain HTML templates.

Beyond the security problems, the personalization has issues:

- **Case mismatch**: `First Name` vs `FirstName`
- **Missing null checks**: `{{Company.Company Name}}` has no fallback
- **Unescaped output**: `$item.manageUrl` should be URL-validated before rendering in `href`
